title: Compounding Risks: Agentic Autonomy Increase × Monitoring Latency — When AI Acts Faster Than Human Review

original_idea.body:
# Compounding Risks: Agentic Autonomy Increase × Monitoring Latency — When AI Acts Faster Than Human Review

**Problem:** As AI agents become more autonomous (HACCA trajectory), the time between a harmful action being initiated and a human reviewer being able to intervene may exceed the action's harm horizon.

**Direction:** For GTG-1002's documented attack timeline (reconnaissance to extraction), estimate the time between AI-initiated actions. Compare this to documented human review latency in AI API monitoring systems. Identify the autonomy threshold at which human review becomes too slow to be a meaningful governance check.

**Why it matters:** Human oversight is a core governance assumption in all frameworks (EU AI Act Art. 14, Anthropic RSP). If autonomy speed exceeds oversight latency, this assumption fails—a compound governance collapse.

**Relevant context:** GTG-1002 timeline; HACCA autonomy trajectory; Kraprayoon governance window; Bengio et al. human oversight provisions.
